Exact output:

Down 3
Down 2
Down 1
Go!
Up 1
Up 2
Up 3

The Down lines execute while recursive calls are being placed on the call stack. No Up line can execute until trace(0) returns. The Up lines then appear in reverse order as the suspended calls resume and the stack unwinds.

answers.author: Champak Roy
answers.content:
A string of length zero or one is already reversed. Reverse everything after the first character, then append the first character.

def reverse_text(text):
    if len(text) <= 1:
        return text
    return reverse_text(text[1:]) + text[0]

print(reverse_text('RECURSION'))  # NOISRUCER

There are n recursive calls. Because Python creates new strings during slicing and concatenation, this direct version can take O(n²) time and space.

answers.author: System Hint
answers.content: For a non-empty string, solve the smaller problem text[1:] and decide where text[0] belongs in the result.

answers.author: Champak Roy
answers.content:
Use the last element as the base case. Compare the current value with the maximum returned for the remaining positions.

def recursive_max(values, index=0):
    if index == len(values) - 1:
        return values[index]

    rest_max = recursive_max(values, index + 1)
    return values[index] if values[index] > rest_max else rest_max

print(recursive_max([7, 2, 19, 4, 11]))  # 19

Complexity: O(n) time and O(n) call-stack space.

answers.author: System Hint
answers.content: Passing an index lets every call move forward without creating a sliced copy of the list.

answers.author: Champak Roy
answers.content:
At each recursion level choose 0, then choose 1. Store the string when its length reaches n.

def binary_strings(n):
    answers = []

    def build(current):
        if len(current) == n:
            answers.append(current)
            return

        build(current + '0')
        build(current + '1')

    build('')
    return answers

print(binary_strings(3))

The recursion tree has 2ⁿ leaves. Producing 2ⁿ strings of length n takes O(n·2ⁿ) time and output space.

answers.author: System Hint
answers.content: The base case is len(current) == n. Before reaching it, make two recursive calls: one after adding 0 and one after adding 1.
